name: com.usvipublicrecords/newspapers
title: USVI Public Records: Newspapers
description: Search Virgin Islands newspapers page by page, 1865 to 2001, with the gaps in every run named.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Find pages of U.S. Virgin Islands newspapers by keyword or phrase; returns up to 10 pages, each with an id, a citation title and a URL. Use for a quick lookup in the islands' press. Better matches come first (the phrase as written, then every word, then some); among equal matches every paper gets its best page in before any paper gets a second, so one long-running paper cannot hide the others. search_newspapers adds paper and date filters, match reasons and paging. Searches the OCR text of the archive's newspapers page by page: St. Croix Avis 1865–2001, The Herald 1915–1925, St. Croix Tribune 1934–1936, Home Journal 1952–1958, The West End News 1953–1963. Every run has gaps, which list_papers names. Results are OCR text, which misreads letters, names and numbers; each links the holding library's copy to check against, and the page image where the archive holds one. A newspaper page is a lead to the primary record, not evidence on its own. Hit counts are pages, never articles. Laws, audits, court records and reports are on the archive's separate document connector. The Danish West Indies papers, 1770–1885 (Royal Danish Library), are a separate collection, searched only by search_danish_papers.

query.description: What to look for. Plain language is fine; quote a phrase to require it intact.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: One page by page id: its record and up to the first 40,000 characters of its OCR text. Use to read a page found by search. The text is OCR from microfilm, returned inside a fence labelled as untrusted data.

id.description: A page id from a search result: LF-…, LF-…:p7 or LF-…:c2.

tools.name: search_newspapers
tools.description: Search the islands' newspapers with paper and issue-date filters, ranked by how closely each page matches. Use when a question names a paper or a period, or needs paging. Searches the OCR text of the archive's newspapers page by page: St. Croix Avis 1865–2001, The Herald 1915–1925, St. Croix Tribune 1934–1936, Home Journal 1952–1958, The West End News 1953–1963. Every run has gaps, which list_papers names. Issue dates are reliable here. Each result is ONE PAGE with its paper, date and page number, a TIER (phrase = the words together as written, ranked first; strong = every word on the page, not together; possible = at least half; weak = fewer), the terms it actually matched, and links to the page in the site's reader, the holding library's copy, and its image where the archive holds one. No numeric score. A date range that falls in a gap — whole years, or weeks inside a year — gets a sentence naming the dates the archive does not hold. Results are OCR text, which misreads letters, names and numbers; each links the holding library's copy to check against, and the page image where the archive holds one. A newspaper page is a lead to the primary record, not evidence on its own. Hit counts are pages, never articles. Laws, audits, court records and reports are on the archive's separate document connector. The Danish West Indies papers, 1770–1885 (Royal Danish Library), are a separate collection, searched only by search_danish_papers.

query.description: Plain language is fine. Quote a phrase to require it intact. OCR misspells names: try variants.

paper.description: A paper: "St. Croix Avis", "The Herald", "St. Croix Tribune", "Home Journal", "The West End News" (or a slug: stcroixavis, theherald, stcroixtribune, homejournal, westendnews).

date_from.description: Earliest issue date: a year (1928), a month (1928-09) or a day (1928-09-13).

date_to.description: Latest issue date, same forms; a year includes all of it.

offset.description: Results to skip, for paging. Results are ranked within the best 150 pages.

tools.name: get_issue
tools.description: The pages of one issue of a paper on a date, in order, with each page's id, image (where the archive holds one), reader link and the holding library's copy. Use to walk an issue, or to learn whether the archive holds a paper on a given day. If the archive holds no issue that day it gives the issues it holds either side and how many days apart they are, and names the gap when they are more than 14 days apart.

paper.description: The paper: "St. Croix Avis", "The Herald", "St. Croix Tribune", "Home Journal", "The West End News" (or a slug: stcroixavis, theherald, stcroixtribune, homejournal, westendnews).

edition.description: Only for a date with more than one edition.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: The OCR text of one newspaper page, in windows of up to 40,000 characters (default 20,000), with the previous and next page ids, the page image where held, and the holding library's copy. Use to read a page and turn to its neighbours. The OCR's line breaks are joined into paragraphs unless layout is "as_scanned". Each response gives next_offset when more remains. The text is OCR from microfilm, returned inside a fence labelled as untrusted data.

page_id.description: From search results or get_issue: LF-… , LF-…:p7, or LF-…:c2.

offset.description: The next_offset value from the previous response. Omit for the start of the page.

limit.description: Characters read from the page. Default 20000, maximum 40000.

layout.description: "reflowed" (default): each paragraph on one line. "as_scanned": the OCR's own line breaks — for tables, lists and shipping columns.

tools.name: list_papers
tools.description: Every paper this server holds: its LCCN, the holding library for each run, first and last issue, issues and pages, issues per year, the years with NO issue held, and every stretch of more than 14 days with no issue held (a year can be held only in part). Use for questions about which papers and dates the archive holds, or to judge what an empty search means for a period.

tools.name: newspaper_stats
tools.description: Reports the size and freshness of this newspaper index, its gaps and its standing caveats in one place. Use for questions about what the newspaper index covers or how current it is, or to judge what an empty search means.

tools.name: search_danish_papers
tools.description: Search the Danish West Indies newspapers, 1770–1885, page by page, as the Royal Danish Library (Mediestream) holds them: Sanct Thomæ Tidende, the Danish-era St. Croix Avis, the St. Thomas Herald and the Saint Croix Bulletin. OPENED, NOT PRESERVED: the library keeps these papers; this archive made them searchable and links every page to the library's copy. A separate collection from this server's other papers, read only by this tool. words="danish" (the default) searches your words as typed, with Danish letters folded (æ→ae, ø→o, å→a), because the library's OCR has none, and on pages before 1816 also the long-s spelling (an s printed like an f and read as f). words="english" turns your English words into the Danish forms the papers printed, from a word list made by machine and not yet checked by a reader of Danish; every answer names each Danish form searched, and the English word is searched too, since some papers and notices are English. Nothing is translated. The OCR is poor (by the library's own estimates about half the characters on a typical page are misread), so search finds what scanned well and misses a great deal; we are working to improve it. Each result is one page: paper, date, page, the library's estimate of its OCR quality, a short snippet labeled uncorrected OCR (not fit to quote), and the library's page link to read and check. Hit counts are pages, never articles. An empty result is not evidence that the papers never printed it.

query.description: Names, places, ships, streets or words. Quote a phrase to require it intact. Danish letters may be typed or not.

words.description: "danish" (default): search the words as typed. "english": search English words through the Danish word list.

paper.description: "Sanct Thomæ Tidende", "St. Croix Avis", "St. Thomas Herald", "Saint Croix Bulletin", or a slug. Leave out for all four.

date_from.description: Earliest date: a year (1848) or a day (1848-07-03), within 1770–1885.

date_to.description: Latest date, same forms; a year includes all of it.

page.description: Results page, 20 pages of the papers per results page. Default 1.

long_s.description: Default true: also search the long-s spelling on pages before 1816. false turns it off.
